# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 10 (Bu-Vb Np10)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Np10
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 10
**Title (English, from literature):** Excessive prompting to get a robe
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin01m.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

 The rule specifies that when money intended for a monk's robe has been placed with a designated steward, the monk may indicate his need up to an allowable limit; if he presses excessively or acts inappropriately to obtain the robe, the robe must be forfeited and the transgression confessed. In addition, the rule formalizes the mechanism through which a lay follower manages funds on behalf of a donor wishing to provide robes for a monk.

In his study of monastic administrative roles, Jonathan A. Silk notes that in Nissaggiya 10 the *veyyāvaccakara* is specifically a lay assistant rather than an ordained monk [Silk 2008]. Silk further notes that in the Vinaya commentary *Samantapāsādikā*, Buddhaghosa defines the *veyyāvaccakara* in this context as a *kiccakara kappiyakāraka*, an attendant who performs necessary tasks and "legalizes" transactions for monastics [Silk 2008].
